overview.description: Machine learning is now a core biotech tool: protein language models (ESM) embed sequences, structure predictors (AlphaFold) fold them, and generative models design new ones. The valuable skill is not running a model but evaluating it honestly - homology-aware splits, sensible baselines, and wet-lab validation.
objectives: use foundation models (ESM embeddings, AlphaFold) as tools
avoid data leakage with homology-aware train/test splits
choose baselines and metrics that actually reflect the biology
treat model output as a hypothesis to validate experimentally, not a result

steps.description: Machine learning is now a core biotech tool: protein language models (ESM) embed sequences, structure predictors (AlphaFold) fold them, and generative models design new ones. The valuable skill is not running a model but evaluating it honestly - homology-aware splits, sensible baselines, and wet-lab validation.
steps.intro: Bio ML rewards skepticism: a model that looks brilliant usually has a leaky split or a too-easy test set - the job is to break your own model before the wet lab does.

instructions.title: Frame the task
instructions.description: Define input->output precisely (function prediction, binder design, property regression) and the biological question it answers.

instructions.title: Split honestly
instructions.description: Cluster by sequence/structure identity and split across clusters so the test set is not a near-duplicate of training (the #1 way bio ML lies).

instructions.title: Baseline & embed
instructions.description: Compare against a simple baseline; use ESM embeddings or structures as features where they help.

instructions.title: Validate wet-lab
instructions.description: Treat top predictions as hypotheses - order and test them, and report real hit rate, not just held-out AUC.

submission.description: Propose an ML task for a biological problem, specify a leakage-proof (homology-aware) evaluation, and describe how you would validate predictions experimentally.
